title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading the Alentejo and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show Alentejo DOC, sometimes a sub-region like Reguengos or Portalegre, or Vinho Regional Alentejano. Reserva in Portugal means higher alcohol and approval by a tasting panel; Garrafeira means longer ageing. Vinho de Talha marks clay-pot wines. Blends are common; grapes may be listed on the back.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Alentejo food is rustic: black pork, porco preto, from acorn-fed pigs; lamb; migas, bread with pork; açorda, bread soup; and sheep's cheese like Serpa. Reds suit pork and lamb; Antão Vaz whites suit bacalhau and grilled fish. Serve reds at 16 to 18, slightly cool in summer.

steps.prompt: Which Alentejo meat is a classic with its reds?
steps.explanation: Acorn-fed black pork suits ripe Alentejo reds.

steps.body: Alentejo reds offer ripe fruit and soft tannins at modest prices, among Portugal's most popular wines at home.

steps.prompt: In Portugal, Garrafeira means longer ageing.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show DOC or Regional, and Reserva or Garrafeira
Reds suit black pork and lamb
Serve reds slightly cool in hot weather
